claim.quote: We report the first measurement of the DVCS beam-spin asymmetry using the CLAS12 spectrometer with a 10.2 and 10.6 GeV electron beam scattering from unpolarised protons.

name: CLAS12 first DVCS beam-spin asymmetry measurement
notes: Preprint dated by arXiv v1; the paper was later published in Phys. Rev. Lett. (2023) according to a search-engine summary, not verified here.

summary.plain: CLAS12's first deeply virtual Compton scattering measurement, using 10.2 and 10.6 GeV electrons on protons. It provides over 2000 new data points that extend far beyond earlier data and tighten constraints on the proton's three-dimensional structure.
summary.technical: First CLAS12 measurement of the DVCS beam-spin asymmetry with 10.2 and 10.6 GeV electron beams on an unpolarised liquid-hydrogen target (data from Fall 2018 and Spring 2019), providing over 2000 new data points that greatly extend the Q^2 and Bjorken-x coverage in the valence region and constrain generalised parton distributions.

title: First CLAS12 measurement of DVCS beam-spin asymmetries in the extended valence region
why_it_matters: DVCS data constrain generalised parton distributions, the 3D structure of the nucleon, over a much larger kinematic range than before.
